patch_description:
Use a radically more parameter-efficient ansatz block built around *global/shared* single-qubit mixers and *one shared* entangling controlled rotation, combined with a fixed hypercube-style CZ entangler (no parameters). The key idea is to reduce the number of trainable circuit parameters per block (improving parameter efficiency and generalization) while still giving enough nonlinearity for the classifier to separate classes. Concretely:
- Apply the same RY and RZ (shared params) to all qubits to create a strong, symmetry-friendly input mixing.
- Use a fixed CZ “hypercube” entangler (no parameters) to inject high-order correlations.
- Add one shared CRZ layer on a disjoint matching to provide a trainable non-diagonal interaction channel.
- Finish with a shared RX “output mixer” to rotate learned correlations into the measured Z basis.
